question: A building finished and placed: CBuildingConstruction::Deliver, CBuildingDeployment (constructor, DeployAt, CanDeployIn), the deploy menu and the map for a building, the message, and the saves.

addresses.name: CBuildingConstruction::Deliver
addresses.comment: **Slot 9: a finished building line delivers one building.** Bare `ret`; CDistributeProduction::Distribute calls it when progress >= duration and removes the line when it answers 1. Read whole on the listing 2026-10-15. In order: (1) a country (+0x48/+0x4C) that is not REB and owns no province (+0xCF8 <= 0) - answer 1 and nothing else. (2) **The practical**: where the building's category (CBuilding +0x88) answers its slot 2 - both CTechnologyCategory and the null category hold `mov al,1; ret` there - CCountry::GainTechAbility(country, category, completion_size (+0x8C)), **in full: no practical_factor**, unlike a unit's. (3) **Where the building is `capital = yes` (+0x60) and the line has no province (+0x44 null)**: a CBuildingDeployment (0x3C bytes, CBuildingDeployment::CBuildingDeployment with the line's country), its id set through slot 6 to (the line's id type +8, the line's id +0xC + count (+0x5C) + 1), its building (+0x38) = the line's, appended to the country's deployments (CCountry_AddDeployment, +0x688), count += 1. **No message.** (4) **Otherwise, where there is a province**: the province's building of that index (+0x310[CBuilding +0x54]) has level_max (+0x20) += 1000, capped at max_level*1000 and floored at 0 - **level_current (+0x24) is not touched**, so the new level works only as the day's repair fills it - then CProvinceBuilding_OnLevelChanged (which does nothing but for infrastructure). For the underground (g_CBuildingDataBase +0x28): level_current += Underground_GetInitialStrength(province, country), capped at level_max, `changed` (+0x28) = whether it moved, underground_owner (+0x38C/+0x390) = the line's country, CCountry_AddUnderground, the template's +0x20 = 1. Then **BUILDING_DONE** where the local player (CCurrentGameState +0xC34) is the province's **controller** (+0x338): variables NAME (the building's slot 6, its name string at +0x38) and PROV (the province's GetName), both shield countries the province's **owner**, and the callback thunk 0x522400 (CInGameIdler slot 78) for its Goto. A non-capital building with no province gets the practical and nothing else. Nothing here refreshes the area's ports and air bases (COwnerArea::RefreshBases is not called), rebuilds the province's modifier, or touches radar. (5) progress -= min(duration, progress); size (+0x40) -= 1; in a custom game at stage 2 (GetCustomGameSettings: byte +0 set, +0x18 == 2) whose list holds the country (CustomGameSettings_HasCountry) the settings' +0x6C = 1; where size is still above 0, slot 14 prices the line again. Answers size <= 0. **Every line priced again** is not here: Distribute does that, with CCountry::RebuildStaticModifiers, on any day a Deliver answered 1 - a unit's line as much as a building's. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-buildingqueue.md, section B.

Wrong if a path through 0x485D46 reached RefreshBases or 0x49F3E0 - no call to either is in the body.

Now read whole: the practical has no practical_factor; `count` numbers the deployments; the deployment path sends no message; level_current is not raised; nothing refreshes the area's bases, the province's modifier or radar; the repricing of every line is Distribute's, on any finished line.

addresses.name: CBuildingDeployment::DeployAt
addresses.comment: **Slot 9: a finished capital building waiting in the deploy menu is put in a province.** `ret 4`. Read whole on the listing 2026-10-15. Notes first whether the province had a working port - owned (+0x330), a CPort (+0x354) and a naval base (+0x300) with level_max above 0 - and whether its underground (+0x30C) had a level_max above 0. Then the building of that index: level_max += 1000, capped at max_level*1000 and floored at 0 (**level_current untouched**, as in CBuildingConstruction::Deliver), CProvinceBuilding_OnLevelChanged. **Where there was no working port and there is one now, COwnerArea::RefreshBases on the province's area** (+0x2B4) - a naval base; an air base appearing refreshes nothing. Where the underground went from no level to a level: level_current += Underground_GetInitialStrength(province, the deployment's country +0x30/+0x34), capped, `changed`, underground_owner = that country, CCountry_AddUnderground, the template's +0x20 = 1. Then **BUILDING_DONE** (NAME = the building's name string, PROV = the province's name) where the local player is the province's controller (+0x338), with the **controller** as the first shield country and the **owner** as the second, and the callback thunk 0x522400. Nothing is asked of the province: CanDeployIn is the caller's business, and CDeployUnitCommand::Execute does not ask it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-buildingqueue.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x57E640-0x57ED7x: `cmp [edi+0x330],ebx`, `cmp [edi+0x354],ebx`, `mov eax,[edi+0x300]; cmp [eax+0x20],ebx; setg [esp+0x13]`; `mov eax,[edi+0x30c]; cmp [eax+0x20],ebx; ... setg [esp+0x1b]`; `add dword [eax+0x20],0x3e8` with the max_level cap; `call 0x4b7fa0`; `cmp byte [esp+0x13],bl; jne` then the same three tests and `mov edi,[edi+0x2b4]; call 0x47e6d0`; `cmp byte [esp+0x1b],bl; jne` and `cmp [eax+0x20],ebx; jle` before `call 0x509230` and `call 0x50a030`; `cmp [eax+0xc34],[edi+0x338]; jne 0x57ed64`; pushes +0x330, +0x32C, +0x338, +0x334 before CMessage::CMessage at 0x57EC37; `mov esi,0x522400`. Wrong if the RefreshBases arm tested +0x304: it reads +0x300 both times.
addresses.revises: Was `inferred` and said the area's bases are refreshed 'where an air base appears'. It is where a naval base makes a port that was not there (+0x300 and the CPort at +0x354); a new air base refreshes nothing. Read whole; the shields are controller and owner.

addresses.name: CBuildingDeployment::CanDeployIn
addresses.comment: **Slot 10: whether a finished building waiting in the deploy menu may be put in a province.** `ret 4`, two exits 0x57E5B7 (false) and 0x57E61F (true). The country is the deployment's (+0x30/+0x34). False, in order: (1) the province has no CPort (+0x354) and the building is `port = yes` (+0x61); (2) CCountry::IsBuildingAllowed(country, building, province) refuses - the call BiceLib hooks at 0x57E4E5 (Hook_PlaceBuildingCheck). Then **the underground** (g_CBuildingDataBase +0x28): false where the province's underground has a level_max above 0; true where the province's controller is at war with the country (CCountry::IsEnemyTag, REB counting), the country is a friend of the province's owner (CCountry::IsFriend with military access), and the country is a major (+0x15C) or has MaxIC (+0x60C) above 100 or owns the province. **Any other building**: false unless the province's controller (+0x338) is the country; a naval base (db +0x20) only where the province's naval base (+0x300) has level_max 0; an air base (db +0x1C) only where its air base (+0x304) has level_max under one whole level; anything else true. So **a deployment can only make a new naval base or air base, never add a level to one**; anti-air, radar, a reactor or a rocket site may go on top of what is there up to max_level. `capital`, `onmap`, `orientation`, `show_for_province`, the owner (but for the underground) and the terrain are not asked. It also colours the map while a deployment is being placed (MapMode_Deployment_Colour) and gates the left click that places it (CInGameIdler_HandleInput). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-buildingqueue.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x57E480-0x57E632: `cmp dword [ebx+0x354],0; jne` / `cmp byte [eax+0x61],0; jne 0x57e5b7`; `push ebx; push ecx; mov ecx,esi; call 0x4dffc0; test al,al; je 0x57e5b7`; `cmp edx,[eax+0x28]; jne 0x57e5cd`; `mov ecx,[ebx+0x30c]; cmp [ecx+0x20],0; jg`; `call 0x42f1b0` and `push 1; lea edx,[ebx+0x32c]; call 0x4ef7c0`; `cmp byte [esi+0x15c],0`, `cmp [esi+0x60c],0x64; jg`, `cmp [ebx+0x330],[esi+0xca8]`; at 0x57E5CD `cmp [ebx+0x338],eax; jne`; `cmp ecx,[eax+0x20]` and `cmp [edx+0x20],0; jne` on +0x300; `cmp ecx,[eax+0x1c]` and the divide by 1000 of +0x304's +0x20 (`imul 0x10624dd3; sar edx,6`) then `jne 0x57e5b7`. vtable.py --holding: slot 10 of CBuildingDeployment only. Wrong if the false exit at 0x57E5B7 were reachable from the naval-base test with a non-zero level - it is the `jne` there.

addresses.comment: **Constructor**, `this` in EAX, the country's tag and id by value on the stack, `ret 8`. Writes CReferenceObject's vftable and its +4 = 0x18D, the default id (+8/+0xC from 0x1A8CC94/0x1A8CC98), an empty string at +0x14 (its byte +0x10), the country at +0x30/+0x34, and CBuildingDeployment's vftable (0x15BDF14). The building (+0x38) is set by the caller. 0x3C bytes, as both callers allocate. Two callers: CBuildingConstruction::Deliver (0x485CCD) and CCountry::LoadKey's `building_deployment` arm (0x4CD950), which passes the loading country.

addresses.name: CCountry_AddDeployment
addresses.comment: Appends a deployment to the back of country->deployments (+0x688, tail +0x68C, count +0x690), a 0x10-byte node {data, prev, next, byte}. `ret 4`. Three callers: CMilitaryConstruction::Deliver (0x485038), CBuildingConstruction::Deliver (0x485CF1) and CCountry::LoadKey (0x4CD918). So the deploy menu lists deployments in the order they were finished. The name is ours.

addresses.name: CCountry::IsBuildingAllowed
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CCountry::IsBuildingAllowed(CCountry* this, CBuilding* building, CProvince* province)
addresses.comment: **Whether a country may have one more of a building in a province** - the Lua API's CCountry:IsBuildingAllowed. `ret 8`. False, in order: (1) the building is not available to the country - TechnologyStatus (+0xDF8)->building_available (+0x28C)[building index], set by a researched technology's `activate_building`; (2) for any building but the underground, the country is not the province's controller (+0x338); (3) **the province's whole levels built (level_max / 1000, truncated) plus the `size` (+0x40) of every line in the country's queue (+0xF40) that is a building line (slot 16) for this province and this building reach max_level (+0x68)**; (4) the province has no CPort (+0x354) and the building is `port = yes`; (5) any building of the resolved not_if_x_exists list (+0xBC) has a level_max above g_FixedZero in the province; (6) any building of the resolved prerequisites list (+0x9C) has none. True otherwise. The owner is not asked, nor `capital`, `onmap`, `orientation` or `show_for_province`. Callers: CBuildingDeployment::CanDeployIn (0x57E4E0), CConstructBuildingCommand::IsValid (slot 14, 0x54562D), CBuildingMember::OnClick (0x6DC0F0, the province view's building button) and that button's update 0x6DC380 twice (0x6DC558, 0x6DC66C). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-buildingqueue.md, sections A and B.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x4DFFC0-0x4E0161: `mov ecx,[edi+0xdf8]; mov edx,[ecx+0x28c]; cmp byte [eax+edx],0; jne`; `cmp ebx,[eax+0x28]; je` / `cmp [edi+0xca8],[edx+0x338]; jne`; `mov ecx,[eax+0x20]; imul 0x10624dd3; sar edx,6` and the loop over +0xF40 `call [edx+0x40]; ... cmp [ebx+0x44],province; cmp [ebx+0x58],building; add esi,[ebx+0x40]`, then `cmp esi,[ebp-0x10]` (max_level from +0x68) `jge false`; `cmp [eax+0x354],0; jne; cmp byte [ebx+0x61],0; jne false`; the +0xBC walk `cmp [ecx+0x20],edi; jg false` and the +0x9C walk `cmp [edx+0x20],edi; jle false` with edi = [0x1A870F4]. Slot 16 is `mov al,1` (0xA92590) on CBuildingConstruction and `xor al,al` (0x592360) on the military and convoy lines. luabind.json names the address. Wrong if (3) counted lines elsewhere: the location and building compares are both there.

addresses.name: CBuilding_ResolveBuildingLists
addresses.comment: **Turns a building's `prerequisites` and `not_if_x_exists` names into buildings**, once each, after buildings.txt is read (its one caller is the loop at 0x4B793F in LoadBuildings, over every building). For each name of the string list at +0xAC: the building of that name (StringHashFind_At1C on the database) is appended to the list at +0x9C; an unknown name is logged "Unknown building '...' referred to in prerequisited list.", the building itself "Building '...' defined as its own prerequisit."; then the string list is freed (0x4B8C10). The same for +0xCC into +0xBC. So the string lists are always empty in a running game, and the resolved lists are what CCountry::IsBuildingAllowed reads. `ret 4` at 0x4B7500. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x4B6EF0-0x4B7500: `mov eax,[edi+0xac]` loop with `call 0x4b8b60`, the 0x10-byte node appended through +0xA0/+0xA4 and `mov [edi+0x9c],eax`; the strings at 0x15C0924/0x15C08FC and 0x15C095C/0x15C0938; `lea eax,[edi+0xac]; push eax; call 0x4b8c10`; the second loop on +0xCC into +0xBC/+0xC0/+0xC4; `call 0x4b8c10` at 0x4B74E4; `ret 4` at 0x4B7500. retsBefore(0x4B6EF0, 0x4B7500) is that one ret. findRefs --callers: 0x4B793F only.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::SetDeploymentBeingPlaced
addresses.comment: **Slot 30: a finished thing from the deploy menu is being put on the map, or no longer is.** `ret 4`. With null: the id at +0x158/+0x15C cleared and slot 99 (PopMapMode) - the map goes back to the mode it was in. With a deployment: slot 98 (PushMapMode) keeps the current mode; the deployment's id goes to +0x158/+0x15C; leaving the air (18) or naval (19) mode takes their icons down; the idler's mode (+0xD34) and the map's (+0x2A90) = **14**; the settings' +0xE7 = 0, layer mask +0xF0 = 0xFFBA and map style +0xF4 = 11; the graphics owner's +0x60F8 = 0; HideProvinceObjects98; **MapMode_Deployment_Colour**; Map_RefreshColourTextures(0); +0x60DC = 1. The same for a unit's deployment as for a building's. Callers: CDeploymentEntry::OnSelect (the deployment), CSideMenuDeploy::Hide and CDeploymentTargetEntry::OnSelect (null), and CInGameIdler_HandleInput (null, after a placing click). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-buildingqueue.md, section B.

addresses.name: MapMode_Deployment_Colour
addresses.comment: **The map's colours while a finished unit or building is being placed** (mode 14). `ret 4`; one caller, CInGameIdler::SetDeploymentBeingPlaced, so the colours are made once when a line is chosen and not again. Nothing where no deployment is being placed (slot 31). For every province object from index 1 (the vector at +0x2C, each with its province at +0xC): grey (0.5, 0.5, 0.5); where the deployment's slot 10 (CanDeployIn) answers yes, (0.5, 0.9, 0.5); and where the deployment is a building's (slot 8 = 0x4B7) and its building is the underground, green = initial / UNDERGOUND_INITIAL_STRENGTH * 0.3 + 0.6 with red and blue 0.5, initial being Underground_GetInitialStrength for the **player's** country - in single precision through doubles. Alpha 1.0 throughout. Written to both words of each province's colour pair. The name is ours.

addresses.evidence: Listing 0x548FF0-0x5490CC: `mov esi,[ebp+8]`; `mov eax,0x4b5; mov [esi+0x2c],eax; mov [esi+0x30],eax`; `mov [esi+0x3c],[ebp+0x10]; mov [esi+0x40],[ebp+0x14]; mov [esi+0x44],[ebp+0x18]; mov [esi+0x48],[ebp+0x1c]; mov [esi+0x4c],[ebp+0x20]; mov [esi+0x50],[ebp+0x24]; mov [esi+0x54],[ebp+0xc]`; `mov dword [esi],0x15c3794`; `mov eax,esi; ret 0x20`. findRefs --callers: six.

addresses.name: CDeployUnitCommand::Execute
addresses.comment: **Slot 6: puts a finished unit or building somewhere.** Bare `ret`. The deployment by the id at +0x44/+0x48; none, nothing. **Where no target unit is found** by the id at +0x4C/+0x50: the deployment's slot 9 (DeployAt) with provinces[+0x54], then it is unlinked from the deployments (+0x688) of the country whose id is at +0x40 and freed through its slot 0. **Where a target is found**: only a unit's deployment (slot 8 answering 0x4B4) is joined to it (CUnitDeployment::JoinUnit, the flag 0); **any other is left where it is**. Nothing asks CanDeployIn, the controller or the owner: the click that posts it is the only check, and the command's slot 14 (0x5495A0) asks only that the deployment exists. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-buildqueue.md, section 7, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-buildingqueue.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x5490D0-0x5492B4: the two FindPersistentById calls; `lea edi,[eax-8]; test edi,edi; jne 0x54926e`; at 0x549201 `mov ecx,[esi+0x54]; mov ecx,[eax+0xb8c][ecx*4]; push ecx; call [edx+0x24]`; `add esi,0x688` on countries[+0x40]; `call 0x5d49d0`; `push 1; call [edx]`; at 0x54926E `call [edx+0x20]; cmp eax,0x4b4; jne 0x5492a2` (the exit) and `push 0; push edi; push country; call 0x5067d0`.
addresses.revises: Comment extended: a found target with a building's deployment does nothing and leaves it; DeployAt gets the province out of the game state's vector; nothing in the command checks where.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler_HandleInput
addresses.comment: **The in-game screen's handler for the mouse and keys over the map**, called once from CInGameIdler::Update (0x656471), `ret 4`. Read only in part. Known arms: the H key (0x6537D2, render_hierarchy, FINDINGS-hierarchy.md); a right click on a province (0x6534E4, FINDINGS-airorders.md section 6); Escape (0x65385D: with something selected, ClearSelection, else 0x66BD10(0)); and **the left button's release over the map with nothing dragged** (0x652B8F: event +0x14 == 1 and the down byte +0x12E0 set; 0x64D850 false): where a deployment is being placed (slot 31) and there is a province under the pointer (+0x1DD0), the deployment's slot 10 (CanDeployIn) for that province; **yes - a CDeployUnitCommand(province, the player, the deployment, no target) is posted and SetDeploymentBeingPlaced(0)**; no - the click goes on as an ordinary click (0x6532AE), with no message, and the deployment stays chosen. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x652B8F-0x652BD2 (`cmp [esi+0x14],1; jne`, `cmp byte [ebx+0x12e0],al; jne`, `call 0x64d850; test al,al; je 0x653256`); 0x653256-0x6532A8 (`call [edx+0x7c]; test eax,eax; je`, `mov eax,[ebx+0x1dd0]`, `mov eax,[eax+0x1df0][esi*4]`, `mov esi,[eax+0xc]`, `call [edx+0x28]; test al,al; jne 0x6538c8`); 0x6538C8-0x653984 (`push 0x58; call new`, the null target 0x1A8CC94/98, +0x158/+0x15C, `call [edx+0x5c]` for the player, `call 0x548ff0`, `call [edx+0x48]` and its +0x38's slot 6 to post, `push 0; call [edx+0x78]`). Inferred: that +0x14 == 1 is the left button rests on FINDINGS-airorders.md's 2 for the right; the rest of the function was not read.

addresses.name: CustomGameSettings_HasCountry
addresses.comment: False where the custom game settings' first byte is clear; otherwise whether the list at CCurrentGameState +0x60 (entries with a country id at +0x24, next at +0x54) holds the country's id. `ret 8`. Used by both Deliver bodies' tails to set the settings' +0x6C byte. What the list is was not read. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x41D470-0x41D55B: `mov eax,[ebp+8]; cmp byte [eax],bl; je false`; `mov eax,[esi+0x60]`; loop `cmp [ecx+0x24],[country+4]; je true; mov eax,[eax+0x54]`; `ret 8`. The caller in CBuildingConstruction::Deliver pushes &line.country (+0x48) and the settings and cleans nothing.

addresses.name: CProvinceBuilding_OnLevelChanged
addresses.comment: 0x4B7FA0-0x4B8296, `ret 4`, `this` on the stack. Runs after a province building's level_max has moved - CBuildingConstruction::Deliver (0x485D41), CBuildingDeployment::DeployAt (0x57E6E2), 0x42CC39 and 0x50BF03. **It does nothing at all unless the building's modifier is MODIFIER_INFRASTRUCTURE** (`definition_ptr(+0x18)->effect(+0xC)->id(+0x24) == 12`, 0x4B7FC4, `jne` to the exit): no other building's level reaches the province's modifier, the area or radar through it. For infrastructure: the province's MaxInfrastructure (+0x5C) = level_max * 1000 / 10000 - the 0.1 of `infrastructure = 0.1` **hardcoded**, where CProvince::LoadKey and SetProvinceBuildingLevel read CBuilding +0x8 effect_size, so a mod changing it on `infra` makes the writers disagree. Where that crosses g_InfraThreshold0_100 (100) or g_InfraThreshold0_200 (200): **UpdateOwnerAreaOfProvince** with the controller (or `---` where it has fallen to 100 or less) - the call the record had as 'a message through 0x47F540' - then DeleteAreaGroups, RebuildAreaGroups, DeleteSupplyGroups and RebuildSupplyGroups; then every distinct owner of a neighbouring province in a real area, and the controller, has its CCountry +0x580 (theatres_dirty) set; and CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot. The name is from the body.
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x4B7FBB-0x4B7FCB: `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; mov eax,[eax+0xc]; cmp dword [eax+0x24],0xc; ... jne 0x4b8286`. 0x4B7FEA-0x4B8024 `imul eax,eax,0x3e8` then the divide by 10000 (0x68DB8BAD, sar 0xC) into [esi+0x5c]; 0x4B8027-0x4B8063 the threshold compares against [0x1A87098] and [0x1A870B4], `mov dword [ebp-0x24],0x2d2d2d`; `call 0x47f540; add esp,0x14` then 0x47FFF0, 0x47FEB0, 0x4807F0, 0x480690. The neighbour walk's list of 0x14-byte nodes of owner tags, the controller first (0x4B80CA); `call 0x402610; mov byte [eax+0x580],1` at 0x4B8263-0x4B8268 for each; `call 0x4a70c0` (CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot) at 0x4B8279.
addresses.revises: Was `likely`. Confirmed on the listing that it does nothing for any building but infrastructure; 0x47F540 is UpdateOwnerAreaOfProvince, not a message; the theatre flags and UpdateSupplyDepot added.

struct_fields.name: country
struct_fields.comment: Whose it is: the tag at +0x30 and the id at +0x34, set by the constructor from the finished line's country (or the loading country). CanDeployIn asks this country's IsBuildingAllowed, and DeployAt makes it the underground's owner.
struct_fields.evidence: CBuildingDeployment::CBuildingDeployment `mov [eax+0x30],[ebp+8]; mov [eax+0x34],[ebp+0xc]`; CanDeployIn `mov eax,[edi+0x34]; mov esi,[edx+eax*4]` and `cmp [ebx+0x338],[edi+0x34]`; DeployAt `mov eax,[esi+0x30]; mov esi,[esi+0x34]; mov [edi+0x38c],eax; mov [edi+0x390],esi`.

struct_fields.name: prerequisite_buildings
struct_fields.comment: **The resolved `prerequisites`**: one node a building (tail +0xA0, count +0xA4, byte +0xA8), made from the names at +0xAC by CBuilding_ResolveBuildingLists after buildings.txt is read. CCountry::IsBuildingAllowed refuses a province where any of them has no built level. Empty in both installs, whose buildings.txt has no `prerequisites`.
struct_fields.evidence: CBuilding_ResolveBuildingLists appends through `mov [edi+0xa0],eax; mov [edi+0xa4],edx; ... mov [edi+0x9c],eax`; IsBuildingAllowed `mov eax,[ebx+0x9c]` then `mov edx,[eax]; mov edx,[edx+0x54]; ... cmp [edx+0x20],edi; jle false`. The constructor zeroes +0x9C/+0xA0/+0xA4 and the byte +0xA8.

struct_fields.name: excluding_buildings
struct_fields.comment: **The resolved `not_if_x_exists`**: one node a building (tail +0xC0, count +0xC4, byte +0xC8), made from the names at +0xCC by CBuilding_ResolveBuildingLists. CCountry::IsBuildingAllowed refuses a province where any of them has a built level above zero. Empty in both installs.
struct_fields.evidence: CBuilding_ResolveBuildingLists `mov esi,[edi+0xc0]` ... `mov [edi+0xc0],eax` ... `mov [edi+0xbc],eax`; IsBuildingAllowed `mov edx,[ebx+0xbc]` and `cmp [ecx+0x20],edi; jg false`.

struct_fields.name: prerequisites
struct_fields.comment: buildings.txt `prerequisites`: a `{ ... }` block whose every word becomes a std::string on a list (tail at +0xb0, count at +0xb4). **Read once and emptied**: CBuilding_ResolveBuildingLists (0x4B6EF0) turns each name into the building of that name on the list at +0x9C - logging an unknown name or the building itself - and frees these strings (0x4B8C10). So it is empty in a running game whatever the file says, and what the game uses is +0x9C.
struct_fields.evidence: CBuilding_ResolveBuildingLists `mov eax,[edi+0xac]` loop with `call 0x4b8b60`, then `lea eax,[edi+0xac]; push eax; call 0x4b8c10`, which frees each string node.
struct_fields.revises: said nothing reads it; the resolver reads it, makes +0x9C of it and frees it

struct_fields.name: not_if_x_exists
struct_fields.comment: buildings.txt `not_if_x_exists`: a `{ ... }` block whose every word becomes a std::string on a list (tail at +0xd0, count at +0xd4). **Read once and emptied**: CBuilding_ResolveBuildingLists (0x4B6EF0) turns each name into the building of that name on the list at +0xBC and frees these strings. So it is empty in a running game, and what CCountry::IsBuildingAllowed reads is +0xBC.
struct_fields.evidence: CBuilding_ResolveBuildingLists `mov eax,[edi+0xcc]; lea ecx,[edi+0xcc]` loop with `call 0x4b8b60`, then `call 0x4b8c10` at 0x4B74E4.

struct_fields.name: count
struct_fields.comment: saved as `count`: **how many CBuildingDeployments the line has made** - CBuildingConstruction::Deliver gives each deployment the id (line id type, line id + count + 1) and then adds one. Only a capital building's line with no province makes them, so it stays 0 on every line that has a location. **Read live**: zero on all 89.
struct_fields.evidence: Deliver 0x485CA2-0x485CF6: `mov ecx,[edi+0xc]; mov edx,[edi+0x5c]; lea eax,[ecx+edx+1]` into the id handed to the deployment's slot 6, and `inc dword ptr [edi+0x5c]` after CCountry_AddDeployment.
struct_fields.revises: the comment gave only the key and the live zero; what it counts is new

struct_fields.name: placing_deployment_type
struct_fields.comment: Type half of the id of the deployment being placed from the deploy menu; the serial half at +0x15C. Set and cleared by SetDeploymentBeingPlaced, read by GetDeploymentBeingPlaced and by the input handler's placing click, which posts it in the CDeployUnitCommand.
struct_fields.evidence: SetDeploymentBeingPlaced `mov [ebx+0x158],[esi+8]` and `mov [ebx+0x158],0`; GetDeploymentBeingPlaced `mov eax,[ecx+0x158]`; CInGameIdler_HandleInput `mov ecx,[ebx+0x158]` at 0x6538FD.

struct_fields.name: placing_deployment_id
struct_fields.comment: Serial half of the id of the deployment being placed; the type half at +0x158.
struct_fields.evidence: SetDeploymentBeingPlaced `mov [ebx+0x15c],esi` (the deployment's +0xC); GetDeploymentBeingPlaced `mov ecx,[ecx+0x15c]`; CInGameIdler_HandleInput `mov edx,[ebx+0x15c]`.

struct_fields.name: map_mode_stack
struct_fields.comment: The map modes to go back to: PushMapMode puts the current one (+0xD34) on the front (tail +0xABC, count +0xAC0), PopMapMode takes the front one off and sets it. Placing a deployment pushes and pops it.
struct_fields.evidence: PushMapMode `mov ebx,[esi+0xab8]` ... `mov [esi+0xab8],eax`, `[esi+0xac0]`, `[esi+0xabc]`; PopMapMode `cmp [edi+0xac0],0`, `mov eax,[edi+0xab8]; mov ebx,[eax]`.
